clue.text: Soldier in wood backing most of motor-racing circuit

indicators.note: backing means the word for a wood is read from the end to the start

parts.note: fir is a tree, and its timber a wood

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the named circuit is dropped

parts.note: Le Mans in France hosts the famous 24-hour motor race

explanation.surface: A soldier hides in a wood behind most of a race track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the S from LE MANS, giving LEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An infantryman armed with a long gun, the classic private soldier of a rifle regiment.

clue.text: Additional clause trapping a plunderer

indicators.note: trapping means the clause word encloses the letter

parts.note: a rider is a clause added to a document

explanation.surface: A legal add-on that catches a looter.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider attacks to steal, a looter.

clue.text: Possibly his catch initially flung in a sort of tank

definitions.text: Possibly his catch initially flung in a sort of tank

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: the Sherman was an American tank of the Second World War

explanation.surface: A man's haul is tossed into a tank, perhaps an aquarium.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes an angler, whose catch may end up in a tank.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler catches fish and may put them in a tank.

clue.text: This writer set up function, circumventing pub ban

indicators.note: circumventing means the other pieces go round the word for pub
set up in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: this writer means the setter, me
to go is to work or function
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A writer sets up an event round a pub that is then banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses ME to EM in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An official order prohibiting trade is a ban.

clue.text: Missile found in East End school?

indicators.note: East End Londoners, Cockneys, drop the H at the start of words

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A projectile turns up in a London school.
explanation.definitionFit: A projectile fired from a bow is a missile.

clue.text: Move to interchange parts of bookies' signalling process

indicators.note: the two halves of the bookies' term swap places, the back half going to the front

parts.note: tic-tac is the hand-signal code British racecourse bookmakers use to pass on odds

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's gesture code is described as a manoeuvre to swap pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: TIC-TAC is the arm-waving code of British racecourse bookmakers; swapping its halves gives TAC TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre, a move made in a game or campaign.

clue.text: Middle East expert condemns abattoirs, having to leave

indicators.note: condemns means the letters are damned and rearranged
leave means the letters of to are taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: A Middle East expert condemns slaughterhouses, having to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Take T and O from ABATTOIRS and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of Arabic language and culture is an expert on the Arab world.

clue.text: One with taking ways, but thick, do we suppose?

definitions.text: One with taking ways, but thick, do we suppose?

parts.words: One with taking ways, but thick, do we suppose?
parts.note: taking ways means stealing, and thick alludes to the saying thick as thieves

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steals has taking ways, and the saying thick as thieves means very close.

clue.text: Beatify unknown saint, one accepted in church

indicators.note: in means the whole is set within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: accepted means the letter for one is taken inside

parts.note: anon is short for anonymous
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An anonymous holy person is admitted to church and raised.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare someone a saint, close kin to declaring them blessed.

clue.text: Fish on lake, landing woman's undies!

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: ling is a sea fish
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: An angler on a lake hooks some women's underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear.

clue.text: Defiance in press employee wanting admission to ministry

parts.note: a sub, short for subeditor, works on a newspaper
ordination is the rite admitting someone to holy orders

explanation.surface: A newspaper worker rebels because they were denied entry into the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to obey authority is the core sense of defiance.

clue.text: European bishop plugs the old argument? It may be raised

indicators.note: plugs means one piece is pushed into a gap in the others

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of the definite article, as in Ye Olde Shoppe
a row is a quarrel
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A European cleric stops an old quarrel, prompting a raised look.
explanation.definitionFit: One lifts the hair above the eye in surprise or doubt, so it is something often raised.

clue.text: Fabulous creature's condition, having flown at first into beam

indicators.note: into means the condition and the initial go inside the word for beam

parts.note: to beam is to grin broadly
if introduces a condition

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of flown

explanation.surface: A mythical beast's state after flying into a roof timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary beast with an eagle's head and a lion's body, so a creature of fable.

clue.text: Possibly an iron ring incorporated in southern dam

indicators.note: incorporated in means the ring shape is set inside the word for dam

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A ring fixed into a dam in the south of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic iron presses creases flat, one example of a device that makes things even.

clue.text: Like one who's lost husband in state shake-up

indicators.note: shake-up means the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A man loses his husband in a political upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lost is unsure which way to go, uncertain and wavering.

clue.text: Does the owner ever forget having such teeth?

definitions.text: Does the owner ever forget having such teeth?

parts.words: Does the owner ever forget having such teeth?
parts.note: the elephant, which proverbially never forgets, owns these long ivory teeth

explanation.definitionFit: Elephants carry long protruding ivory teeth, and they proverbially never forget.

clue.text: Fellow pinching abandoned car is church officer

indicators.note: pinching means the man's name grips the jumbled letters

parts.note: Stan is a man's name

indicators.note: abandoned means wild, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man steals an abandoned car and turns out to be a church official.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristan looks after a church's vestments and sacred vessels.

clue.text: Biblical sectarian who's audibly dejected, you understand

indicators.note: audibly means the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: dejected means sad, and you understand is you see

explanation.surface: A biblical figure explains that he is sad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sadducees were a Jewish sect in the time of Jesus, opponents of the Pharisees.

clue.text: Record of gangster provided with a new name

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: A dossier on a mobster who has been given a fresh identity.
explanation.walkthrough: Annals are records year by year; the singular is rare but valid.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a yearly chronicle, a written account of events kept as history.

clue.text: Utterance of person short of hairspray?

indicators.note: utterance means the word is said aloud

parts.note: one who lacks something

explanation.surface: Someone short of hairspray says so.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer was a common name for hairspray.

clue.text: Seaside swimmer a woman left to avoid

parts.note: she is a pronoun for a woman
to duck is to dodge

explanation.surface: A woman at the beach goes swimming after leaving to dodge someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelduck is a coastal bird that paddles on estuaries, a waterfowl of the shore.

clue.text: Titled widow regularly heard upholding party wit

indicators.note: upholding in a down clue means the second part sits below

parts.note: a do is a party
a wag is a joker

indicators.note: regularly takes alternate letters

explanation.surface: A noble widow is heard at a party sharing jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow with a title from her late husband.

clue.text: Assiduous searcher's rights to dip into stretches of poetry

indicators.note: to dip into means the abbreviations are placed inside the poetry word

parts.note: feet are units of metre in verse
R abbreviates right, twice for rights

explanation.surface: A researcher's rights to read sections of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferret is to search diligently, so a ferret is a tenacious searcher.

clue.text: Shortfall here in Paris requiring adroit cover-up

indicators.note: cover-up means the word for adroit wraps around the French word

parts.note: deft means skilful
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: A clever deception in Paris needs money to cover a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is the amount by which something falls short, such as money.

clue.text: Foremost duke entertaining king

indicators.note: entertaining means holding inside

parts.note: dukes is old slang for fists
R abbreviates rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A leading duke plays host to a king.
explanation.definitionFit: First means foremost, at the front.

clue.text: Business directions concealed within neat wrapper?

parts.note: Co. abbreviates company

indicators.note: within means the word for concealed sits between the two compass points

parts.note: W and E are west and east
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: Company instructions hidden inside a tidy package.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an old word for cattle, so a neat wrapper is a cow's skin; it is not the adjective tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means cattle, so the covering of one of these beasts is the leather from a cow.

clue.text: Carp caught in Majorca village

indicators.note: caught in means the letters are held inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A fish is caught in a Spanish island village.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to quibble, the sense of cavil.

clue.text: I'm craving a tour round cape, perhaps — and much else!

definitions.text: I'm craving a tour round cape, perhaps — and much else!

parts.note: C abbreviates cape on maps

indicators.note: round signals that the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone longs to travel around a headland, and much more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: The C from 'cape' leads, then IRCUMNAVIGATOR is the anagram of I'M CRAVING A TOUR; the whole clue describes a sailor going round capes and everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sailing all the way round the globe passes many headlands and everything else.

clue.text: Drug that's illegal at English transport caff?

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Ry abbreviates railway

explanation.surface: Illegal drugs at an English roadside café for lorry drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: A transport caff is a British roadside café for lorry drivers; 'transport' leaves the definition to give RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A caff is British slang for a cheap café, a place where people go to dine.

clue.text: Instrument used in recital broadcast about noon

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the single letter
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An instrument played in a broadcast recital at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns RECITAL into CLARIET, and 'about' puts it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind with a single reed, a musical instrument.
